crossrefs.text: They set out from Etham and turned back to Pi-hahiroth, opposite Baal-zephon, and they camped near Migdol.
They set out from Pi-hahiroth and crossed through the sea, into the wilderness, and they journeyed three days into the Wilderness of Etham and camped at Marah.
This is the word that came to Jeremiah concerning all the Jews living in the land of Egypt—in Migdol, Tahpanhes, and Memphis—and in the land of Pathros:
The God of the people of Israel chose our fathers. He made them into a great people during their stay in Egypt, and with an uplifted arm He led them out of that land.
On the fifteenth day of the first month, on the day after the Passover, the Israelites set out from Rameses. They marched out defiantly in full view of all the Egyptians,
But the LORD said to Moses, “Now you will see what I will do to Pharaoh, for because of My mighty hand he will let the people go; because of My strong hand he will drive them out of his land.”
So it shall serve as a sign on your hand and a symbol on your forehead, for with a mighty hand the LORD brought us out of Egypt.”
Pharaohʼs chariots and army He has cast into the sea; the finest of his officers are drowned in the Red Sea.
Do not be afraid of them, for the LORD your God Himself will fight for you.”
For the LORD your God goes with you to fight for you against your enemies, to give you the victory.”
“and you have seen everything that the LORD your God has done to all these nations for your sake, because it was the LORD your God who fought for you.

You need not fight this battle. Take up your positions, stand firm, and see the salvation of the LORD on your behalf, O Judah and Jerusalem. Do not be afraid or discouraged. Go out and face them tomorrow, for the LORD is with you.’”
The LORD your God, who goes before you, will fight for you, just as you saw Him do for you in Egypt

You need not fight this battle. Take up your positions, stand firm, and see the salvation of the LORD on your behalf, O Judah and Jerusalem. Do not be afraid or discouraged. Go out and face them tomorrow, for the LORD is with you.’”
One of you can put a thousand to flight, because the LORD your God fights for you, just as He promised.
For the Lord GOD, the Holy One of Israel, has said: “By repentance and rest you would be saved; your strength would lie in quiet confidence— but you were not willing.”
But the LORD said to Joshua, “Stand up! Why have you fallen on your face?
Get up, for this matter is your responsibility, and we will support you. Be strong and take action!”
So Ezra got up and made the leading priests, Levites, and all Israel take an oath to do what had been said. And they took the oath.
In all their distress, He too was afflicted, and the Angel of His Presence saved them. In His love and compassion He redeemed them; He lifted them up and carried them all the days of old.
Now go, lead the people to the place I described. Behold, My angel shall go before you. But on the day I settle accounts, I will punish them for their sin.”

And I will harden Pharaohʼs heart so that he will pursue them. But I will gain honor by means of Pharaoh and all his army, and the Egyptians will know that I am the LORD.” So this is what the Israelites did.
And the LORD hardened the heart of Pharaoh king of Egypt so that he pursued the Israelites, who were marching out defiantly.
Then Moses cried out to the LORD, “What should I do with these people? A little more and they will stone me!”
who sent His glorious arm to lead them by the right hand of Moses, who divided the waters before them to gain for Himself everlasting renown,
At the blast of Your nostrils the waters piled up; like a wall the currents stood firm; the depths congealed in the heart of the sea.
He turned the sea into dry land; they passed through the waters on foot; there we rejoiced in Him.
By faith the people passed through the Red Sea as on dry land; but when the Egyptians tried to follow, they were drowned.
He turned the sea into dry land; they passed through the waters on foot; there we rejoiced in Him.
But the Israelites had walked through the sea on dry ground, with walls of water on their right and on their left.
For when Pharaohʼs horses, chariots, and horsemen went into the sea, the LORD brought the waters of the sea back over them. But the Israelites walked through the sea on dry ground.
For the LORD your God dried up the waters of the Jordan before you until you had crossed over, just as He did to the Red Sea, which He dried up before us until we had crossed over.

notes.title: Baptized into Moses in the cloud and the sea

crossrefs.text: Jesus performed this, the first of His signs, at Cana in Galilee. He thus revealed His glory, and His disciples believed in Him.
He led them safely, so they did not fear, but the sea engulfed their enemies.
Yet He saved them for the sake of His name, to make His power known.
He saved them from the hand that hated them; He redeemed them from the hand of the enemy.
And as for you, lift up your staff and stretch out your hand over the sea and divide it, so that the Israelites can go through the sea on dry ground.
and the Israelites went through the sea on dry ground, with walls of water on their right and on their left.

When the priests carrying the ark of the covenant of the LORD came up out of the Jordan and their feet touched the dry land, the waters of the Jordan returned to their course and overflowed all the banks as before.
He rebuked the Red Sea, and it dried up; He led them through the depths as through a desert.
